video_script.title: The Rancher's Arithmetic and the Corn Belt's Rain
video_script.hook: Cattlemen protect their breeding cows above all else — they're the "factories" that produce next year's calves.
body_slides: She's worth more than the pickup. Than the land.
Eight hundred miles north, corn futures drop on rain.
The herd is smaller than it's been since 1951.
video_script.voiceover_text: Ranchers protect their breeding cows at all costs. They call them factories because without her today, there's no calf next year. She's worth more than the pickup. Than the land. Eight hundred miles north, corn futures drop on rain. The herd is smaller than it's been since 1951. Weather doesn't follow borders. Markets do. video_script.title: The Moratorium That Came Too Late
video_script.hook: The Canadian fisheries minister called it a two-year pause in 1992.
body_slides: Two years, they said. Just a pause.
The ocean doesn't negotiate with politicians.
Thirty years later, the fish never returned.
video_script.voiceover_text: A security guard wedged a chair through door handles to keep angry fishers out. The year was 1992. Canada's fisheries minister had just announced a two-year pause on cod fishing. Two years, they said. Just a pause. The ocean doesn't negotiate with politicians. Thirty years later, the fish never returned. The moratorium became permanent by accident. Follow for more stories like this at The Docket.
